title: The actual finite tower pullback preserves arbitrary K-flat complexes
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell and a scheme morphism f:X to Y, with coefficients and schemes in universe u [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme]. For n a natural number let B_{W,n} be the constant coefficient ring sheaf O_E/varpi^(n+1) on the small pro-etale site of W. Use the module categories normalizedDVRModules, with object/morphism/module universes u+1/u/u+1, and integralOperationsLevelPullback, the actual chosen left adjoint to coefficientProEtaleModuleDirectImage with its canonical constant-section ring map [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. If P is any unbounded integer-indexed K-flat cochain complex of B_{Y,n}-modules, then termwise application of integralOperationsLevelPullback gives a K-flat B_{X,n}-module complex [def-pc-kflat-complex]. K-flat means the signed direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic complex in this full module universe is acyclic. There is no boundedness, flat-term, constructibility, completeness or ell-invertibility hypothesis. This is a finite-level statement; no sequence complex or sequence evaluation comparison occurs in its conclusion.

source.place: Tags 0DEN and 0DEP; arbitrary K-flat pullback via conservative points, and ordinary scalar extension. Instantiation to the specified finite constant-coefficient adjunction.

proof.text: Fix the coefficient universe u+1 and use the actual algebraic inverse image of ring and module sheaves along the pro-etale geometric morphism. The proved inverseImageOfUniverses helper in the ringed-topos K-flat module transports its underlying-sheaf presentation to the equal ring/module universe; its module functor is still the actual proEtaleModuleInverseImage. Choose the conservative set-indexed family of points on X. The stalk criterion for algebraic inverse image proves K-flatness of the image of P without a flat-term hypothesis.

Extend scalars along the specified constant-ring identification from the inverse-image ring to the target coefficient ring. Arbitrary K-flatness is preserved by scalar extension; no flatness of that ring map is assumed.

The adjunct of the constant-ring identification is the actual constant-section coefficient map: apply the adjunction Hom equivalence to its inverse. Thus pushforwardCongr identifies the composite right adjoint with coefficientProEtaleModuleDirectImage. Uniqueness of left adjoints yields a natural module isomorphism from inverse image followed by scalar extension to integralOperationsLevelPullback. Apply it degreewise and use tensor functoriality to transport acyclicity of every test tensor, proving the claimed K-flatness.

theorem completedTowerFinitePullbackKFlat {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ)
    (P : CochainComplex (normalizedDVRModules l E Y n) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (J := ProEt.topology Y) (R := integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E Y n) P) :
    CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (J := ProEt.topology X) (R := integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E X n)
      (((integralOperationsLevelPullback l E f n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
